tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use when a customer reports...'), focuses on symptom/intent-level triggers (ingest failures, 401/403, egress 4xx/5xx, player 404s, origin latency, etc.) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists trigger contexts including non-obvious ones (CDNAuthorizationStatus, ForceEndpointError, harvest jobs), and explicitly carves out boundaries to other related skills (medialive, mediatailor, cloudfront). It is a moderately long paragraph but stays within reasonable bounds for a complex, multi-service domain with disambiguation needs.
tests.evidence: "Use when a customer reports a MediaPackage problem or when evidence points at the packaging/origin layer: ingest failures or 401/403/SigV4 errors, egress 4xx/5xx, player 404s, origin latency..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into MediaPackage-specific procedures, CLI commands, metric names, and diagnostic trees without explaining general concepts like what HTTP status codes or CloudWatch are. It assumes AWS/CLI familiarity and focuses on domain-specific, non-obvious facts.
tests.evidence: "v2 channels use SigV4 authentication (no per-endpoint credentials). The IngestEndpoints[] array provides the ingest URLs."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus

tests.evidence: "CloudWatch dimension keys are case-sensitive. When querying by output format, try both OutputType and OuputType defensively until AWS resolves the typo."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigation procedure (version detection, ingest/egress analysis, diagnosis trees) applicable to any MediaPackage channel, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: "This skill auto-detects whether the resource is v1 or v2 and branches into the appropriate diagnostic path."
